evidence: Prince Paul produced De La Soul's entire debut album '3 Feet High and Rising' (Tommy Boy, 1989), documented on the album's own production credits and repeated in every standard account of the record, including Paul's own interviews describing the sessions.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Stetsasonic's own records are dense but conventional boom-bap. On De La Soul's album the same production instincts turn playful and collage-like: skits, game-show samples and non-sequitur interludes across a much wider, weirder crate of source records than Paul had used behind Stetsasonic's own mic.

explanation.age7: Prince Paul was the DJ who built the music behind De La Soul's whole first album, mixing lots of different old records together.
explanation.age13: Prince Paul had been DJing for the group Stetsasonic when he heard De La Soul's demo tape and offered to produce their whole debut, '3 Feet High and Rising' (1989). It became one of the most acclaimed hip-hop albums ever made.
explanation.adult: Paul's move from Stetsasonic's DJ booth to producing De La Soul's full debut is the clearest single production credit in this batch: a named producer, a named label, a released record everyone agrees on.
